newsitem.title: USA: Rubin unveils U.S. tax simplification proposals.
newsitem.headline: Rubin unveils U.S. tax simplification proposals.

text.p: Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin on Monday unveiled some 60 proposals for "simplifying" the U.S. tax system that he said would neither increase taxes nor raise the government's spending deficit.
In a briefing for reporters, Rubin said the package will save citizens and small businesses millions of hours spent filling out tax forms.

In addition, he said the government will explore ways to move to an electronic tax payment system to permit taxpayers to pay their tax liabilities by using credit cards, debit cards or other electronic-fund transfer alternatives.
Rubin also issued a statement by President Clinton, who said that the task of filing taxes had become too complex for too many Americans.
"This tax simplifcation plan will begin to ease that burden, particularly for families with children and for small businesses," Clinton said.

Under the proposals, 95 percent of corporations would no longer have to calculate the complex "alternative minimum tax" since corporations with gross receipts below $5 million would be exempt from this task.

In addition, the administration said more than 1.7 million dependents, mostly children, who have $700 or more of earned income would no longer have to file taxes just because they have unearned income.
